text:
aj: Heads up — seeing a latency/cpu spike when the runtime switches active kernels from FP8 -> INT8 under continuous batching. Looks like kernel spin-up + KV cache padding duplicates a memcpy path and stalls the batcher for ~12–30ms depending on sequence shapes.

maria: repro steps? which model and config?

aj: small repro (local): model=redwood-serve-small, batcher=continuous, target_seq=1024, quant_profile=auto-calib FP8->INT8 path. Run load at ~1200 reqs/s with variable seq lengths.

aj: profiling snippet (CPU timeline from perf traces):
```
[spinup] kernel_select() -> load_kernel(INT8-shape-256x64)
memcpy(kv_slab)  8.7ms
prepare_kv_view   3.1ms
batcher_pause     12.4ms
fallback_to_spmm  5.0ms
```

kevin: can you attach the perf trace link? maybe the allocator is misaligned for INT8 slabs so memcpy becomes O(n) hot.

aj: uploaded to perf: https://perf.internal/r/abcd1234 (ci-bot shows trace summary)

ci-bot: Trace abcd1234 uploaded by aj — peak latency 142ms, 95p 98ms, big tail coincident with kernel switch events.

nora: this sounds like the padding heuristic is creating large KV slabs when shapes change. Are we reusing a single slab per model version? If so, repeated resizes can cause copies.

maria: also check quant calibration: the auto-calib path currently rebuilds scales and falls back to a slower packing kernel until the next warmup. If padding interacts with that (different kernel shape) it could force a memcpy path.

kevin: suggestion: add a short pre-warm for upcoming target shape families. When a new shape is selected, pre-allocate aligned slab and pre-touch memory on the worker thread, then swap in without blocking batcher. Also consider shape-class cache so kernels for 256x64 / 512x64 are kept hot.

aj: tried a quick patch that preallocates aligned slab and memtouch on a background thread. Reduced stall from ~12ms -> ~2ms in local. But we still see extra branches in kernel selector when quant_profile changes.

maria: can you share the selector decision log? Need to confirm whether selector is doing a full feature compare and recompiling kernels on minor quant param diffs.

aj: log excerpt: "selector: shape=256 pad=32 quant=auto-calib(scale=0.128, mode=perchannel) -> choose INT8_pack_v2" then immediately later: "quant_update: mode=pertensor -> choose INT8_pack_v1; compile fallback". So tiny quant representation differences are flipping compiled kernel variants.

nora: that's bad. We should normalize quant meta to shape-agnostic buckets before comparing. e.g., quant_bucket = round(scale, 2) or mapping to (FP8-like, INT8-like, 4bit-like) tiers. That avoids churn.

kevin: agree. Also add a TTL for kernel eviction so we don't evict and recompile during bursty traffic. Maybe 5 minutes.

maria: action items: 1) add shape-class slab pre-warm + memtouch (aj) 2) normalize quant meta in selector (nora) 3) TTL for compiled kernels (kevin) 4) telemetry delta to detect kernel_swap stalls (maria)

aj: I'll open a single perf-issue and link the trace + quick patch. assigning to self for pre-warm.

aj: quick note: the pad-trim heuristic should prefer trimming excess prefix padding for continuous batching when quant switch happened recently. That reduces slab growth.

nora: also check KV cache alignment: if slab_base % 64 != 0 we sometimes create an extra aligned copy for GPU DMA. Ensure allocator uses 256B alignment for INT kernels.

kevin: could be hardware-specific. On Ampere we saw DMA penalties for unaligned host pinned buffers. Add a small check in allocator for pinned-host fallback.

maria: I'll add a perf alarm rule: if kernel_swap_count > 5 in 30s and avg_stall_ms > 5 then fire P0 perf-batch alert.

aj: thanks — will push pre-warm PR to draft. If this helps, we can roll patch to canary and observe 95p tail.

kevin: one more thought — quant calibration should be deferred until model is warmed. Instead of immediate recalibration that forces kernel change, queue it and apply during low-load windows or after a threshold of stable shape occurrences.

maria: agreed. Queueing plus normalized quant buckets + TTL should stop churn.

ci-bot: Issue created: PERF-1427 "kernel spin-up + KV slab padding on quant switch" assigned to aj, linked trace abcd1234.

aj: good. I'll update thread with results after canary. Thanks all :rocket:
